key_insight: Physics-constrained causal discovery can distinguish constitutive mechanisms from correlated environmental effects when trained on controlled interventions rather than observational data alone.
engineering_relevance: The approach supports constitutive models that generalize to unseen climates using full-field displacement measurements, without requiring measured stresses or internal variables.
method: Embed balance laws and constitutive skeletons in time-unrolled causal graphs scored by weak-form equilibrium gaps.
Use adaptive lasso and a NOTEARS-type acyclicity constraint to select mechanism dependencies and their evaluation order.
Use automatic differentiation to compute a local identifiability certificate and guide greedy D-optimal test design.
evidence_signal: In a synthetic plate study with 0.01-pixel displacement noise, interventional data recovered the exact 8-edge graph in 7 of 10 runs and kept unseen-climate errors within 3.2%, while strongly confounded observational data failed graph recovery and produced errors up to 41.5%.
watch_item: Evidence is synthetic, and noise-induced bias in the weak-form score remains a primary limitation.
paper_title: Physics-constrained differentiable causal discovery of constitutive mechanisms through boundary value problems
